title: In vitro co-culture and analysis of patient-derived leukemia cells
author: Parker, Hockney, et al.
materials:
Timing: 15 min
1.Preparation of CTV Reagents.a.Remove a vial containing of CTV Violet from the freezer and centrifuge using brief pulses to ensure that lyophilized pellet constituents did not remain stuck to the cap.b.Add 20 μL of DMSO to the CTV, thoroughly mix the contents by vortexing and centrifuge using a brief pulse.
CRITICAL: CTV is light-sensitive and must be stored in the dark. All steps containing CTV need to be conducted in the absence of light.
2.Preparation of Hoechst Pyronin Y Reagents.a.Dissolve Hoechst 3342 powder in sterile distilled water (dH2O) to create a stock concentration of 1 mg/mL. Before each staining protocol, dilute the stock Hoechst 3342 in pre-warmed patient-derived cell media (PDX-ALL media) to obtain a final working Hoechst 33342 concentration of 10 μg/mL.CRITICAL: Hoechst is light-sensitive and therefore all steps containing Hoechst must be conducted in the absence of light.CRITICAL: Store 1 mg/mL of Hoechst 33342 stock in −20°C as 1 mL aliquots. Do not repeatedly thaw/re-freeze vials. Store a thawed vial at 4°C and use within 1 week.b.Dissolve Pyronin Y in sterile dH20 to create a stock concentration of 0.1 g/mL. Dilute further in pre-warmed patient-derived cell media (PDX-ALL media) to create a final experimental concentration of 100 μg/mL.CRITICAL: Store stock Pyronin Y in a −20°C freezer in 1 mL aliquots. Store experimental aliquots of 100 μg/mL at 4–8°C, for a maximum of 4 weeks.

steps.title: Validate and isolate cell samples
steps.instruction: Confirm that PDX‑ALL cells are CD45⁺ and CD19⁺ by staining with human‑specific antibodies; if needed, purify CD19⁺ cells by fluorescence‑activated cell sorting. Isolate MSC from patient bone marrow, verify expression of CD105, CD90, CD73 and lack of CD45.

steps.title: Prepare CellTrace Violet reagent
steps.instruction: Retrieve the CellTrace Violet (CTV) vial from the freezer, briefly centrifuge to free any pellet stuck to the cap, add 20 µL DMSO, vortex to mix, and give a brief centrifugation pulse. Keep all steps in darkness because CTV is light‑sensitive.

steps.title: Prepare Hoechst 33342 stock and working solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve Hoechst 33342 powder in sterile distilled water to a 1 mg/mL stock; aliquot 1 mL, store at –20 °C. Thaw an aliquot, keep at 4 °C and use within 1 week. Immediately before staining, dilute the stock in pre‑warmed PDX‑ALL media to a final concentration of 10 µg/mL. Perform all steps protected from light.

steps.title: Prepare Pyronin Y stock and working solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve Pyronin Y in sterile distilled water to a 0.1 g/mL (100 mg/mL) stock; aliquot 1 mL and store at –20 °C. Dilute the stock in pre‑warmed PDX‑ALL media to a final experimental concentration of 100 µg/mL and keep at 4–8 °C for up to 4 weeks. Protect from light.

steps.title: Set up MSC‑PDX‑ALL co‑culture
steps.instruction: Count PDX‑ALL cells and seed them with MSC at 0.5 × 10⁶ cells/mL. Prepare two arms: an untreated control and a 10 nM dexamethasone‑treated arm. Incubate plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 5 days.

steps.title: Harvest and stain cells with Hoechst/Pyronin Y
steps.instruction: Collect 1 × 10⁶ PDX‑ALL cells from each co‑culture, filter through a 40 µm strainer, and centrifuge at 300 × g (≈1500 RPM) for 5 min. Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL PDX‑ALL media containing 10 µg/mL Hoechst 33342 and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 45 min. Add 5 µL of 100 µg/mL Pyronin Y directly to the Hoechst‑stained cells, mix gently, keep the stained cells on ice and protected from light until acquisition.

steps.title: Acquire Hoechst/Pyronin Y flow data
steps.instruction: Set up the BD FACS Canto II (or compatible BD LSR / Cytek Aurora) following the manufacturer SOP. In the Cytometer window set FSC/SSC to linear scale and fluorescence to linear scale. Load the stained sample tube onto the Sample Injection Tube (SIT), select low flow rate, enable SIT flush, and acquire 10 000 events. Adjust FSC/SSC voltages to gate intact ALL cells, then acquire Hoechst and Pyronin Y fluorescence. Record the data and export the file as an FCS file to a USB drive.

steps.title: Analyze Hoechst/Pyronin Y data
steps.instruction: Open FCS Express 7 Plus (or FlowJo) and create a new layout. Load the exported FCS file, gate intact cells (FSC‑H vs FSC‑A), gate single cells (FSC‑H vs FSC‑A), and gate live cells (PI‑negative). Plot Hoechst‑A vs Pyronin Y‑A and apply a quad gate: Q4 = G0, Q1 = G1, Q2 = S/G2. Display a Hoechst histogram to visualise DNA content. Save the analysis.

steps.title: Acquire CTV proliferation flow data
steps.instruction: Set up the FACS Canto II as before. Load the CTV‑labeled PDX‑ALL sample tube, set FSC/SSC voltages to select intact cells, and use the 405 nm violet laser to detect CTV fluorescence. Acquire 10 000 events, record the data, and export as an FCS file.

steps.title: Analyze CTV proliferation data
steps.instruction: Open FCS Express 7 Plus, create a new layout and import the CTV FCS file. Gate intact cells, single cells, and live (PI‑negative) cells. Plot FSC‑A vs CTV‑A; cells retaining high CTV intensity appear on the right, while proliferating cells shift left. Generate a CTV‑A histogram, fit the proliferation model, and obtain statistics for each generation.

description: Here we describe the specific steps used on PDX-ALL cells in co-culture with human MSC (CD105+CD90+CD73+CD45- MSCs, that can differentiate into osteoblasts, adipocytes and chondrocytes), and label PDX-ALL cells in vitro with CellTrace Violet, and Hoechst-33342 and Pyronin Y staining to determine cell cycling and quiescence. This protocol has also been used on PDX-ALL cells, namely samples L707R(relapse) and L707, L49120, MS40, L4967, and ALL cell lines, HAL-01, SEM and PreB697 and AML cell lines, MOLM-14, MV4-11 and Kasumi-1. PDX-ALL samples obtained from mice were confirmed to be positive for hematopoietic marker CD45 and lymphoid marker CD19 using relevant human-specific antibodies. Where relevant a purification using human CD19 antibody was performed using fluorescence-assisted cell sorting (FACS). MSC were isolated as described in previous studies,3 from bone marrow of patients undergoing total hip replacements and were confirmed to express CD105, CD90, CD73 and show absence of hematopoietic marker CD45. This protocol has also been reproduced using ALL and AML co-cultures with different human feeder types including primary human MSC, and induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) derived MSC and angiogenic cells. Angiogenic cells refer to a combination of iPSC-derived endothelial and perivascular cells. Co-culture methods used here are as described in previous studies.1,3
